what: Plan section 7.32, not blind: the v2.2 rule 12 and v2.5 rule 3 post-checks narrowed; stage 1 keeps fee amounts defined under other names, abbreviated MAE terms, 'deemed to have a Material Adverse Effect' definitions, and undefined-MAE paragraphs in any party's representations when no MAE is defined; schema v2.16 (four rulings); MAE (and for a0e138bb and 9dae91bb the fees) re-extracted for all 50 M13 agreements and the 10 M11 and M12 agreements whose candidates changed; M11 to M13 and the 342-agreement pool re-scored against the same final gold.
postcheck_audit: M11 to M13 (per-agreement data for older holdouts is not kept): v2.2 rule 12 drops 0a91852c (wrong) and keeps 4 correct M12 fires; v2.5 rule 3 drops de5d8138 (wrong) and keeps af7f15bd (correct)

stage1.tried_and_reverted: letting an MAE definition run on across a page-break section boundary: it changed 8 more agreements and gained no gold quote (10eaf6ad's definition starts on a page missing from the text)

m12holdout.correct_value: announcement_or_pendency, buyer_action_or_request, change_in_gaap, change_in_law, compliance_with_agreement, general_economic
m12holdout.reason: Carve-out (c) is a single phrase, 'changes in general economic conditions affecting banks and their holding companies generally'; under v2.3 rule 11, general economic conditions in the target's industry are general_economic only, and industry is added only for a separate industry carve-out, which this definition lacks.

m13holdout.correct_value: gold's eight visible carve-outs (b)-(i) (industry, natural_disaster, political_war_terrorism, change_in_law, change_in_gaap, announcement_or_pendency, other, financial_markets, compliance_with_agreement, buyer_action_or_request) with the disproportionate-effect proviso reaching (a)-(e) and (g)
m13holdout.reason: The surviving part of the definition (Exhibit A-11, S121) lists carve-outs (b) to (i) and a proviso for clauses (a) through (e) and (g); the candidate copy of S121 holds only the marker, without that paragraph, so the extractor coded no carve-outs. Nothing in v2.16 changes gold's coding.

The Purchaser has no defined MAE term, and its non-contravention rep 2.2(b) (S10, in the candidates) uses 'a material adverse effect on the Purchaser's ability to perform its obligations hereunder' operatively, which adds a buyer_side entry under v2.15 rule 1; v2.16 does not change this.

m13holdout.correct_value: gold's categories, including other on carve-out (d) in both definitions
m13holdout.reason: Carve-out (d) also excludes 'any Government Shutdown, any declaration of martial law or similar directive ... or other action by any Governmental Authority', which no listed code covers, so 'other' belongs beside natural_disaster and pandemic (and in the disproportionate-effect list) in both definitions.

Carve-out (b) excludes changes in third-party payor and accreditation requirements 'that are generally applicable to hospitals or health care facilities', an industry-wide change that no law code fits, so the listed code industry fits better than other (close call; gold kept clause (a) as change_in_law because a law code fits there).

v2.16 changes the answer: 'Material Adverse Effect' is defined in two separate sentences, one 'With respect to Parent' and one 'With respect to the Company', each stating its own business-and-prospects test, so v2.16 rule 3 makes it one entry per party (buyer_side and target_side). Gold, coded as one 'both' entry under v2.15 rule 2, was fixed to two entries.

Sections 3.1 and 4.1 (S13, S34, both in the candidates) define 'ETP Material Adverse Effect' and 'ETE Material Adverse Effect' on the generic Person-based definition in 8.13, so v2.15 rule 2 gives one entry per party-specific term and none for the generic term, which is not used on its own; v2.16 does not change this.

m13holdout.correct_value: announcement_or_pendency, buyer_action_or_request, change_in_gaap, change_in_law, compliance_with_agreement, failure_to_meet_projections, general_economic, industry, labor, natural_disaster, other, political_war_terrorism
m13holdout.reason: Carve-out (h) covers announcement effects 'including any employee departures', a workforce effect that the M11 and M12 precedents code as labor beside announcement_or_pendency; each clause takes every category it covers. Not a v2.16 change; gold updated.

Clause (a) is 'general economic conditions in the industries or markets in which the Company ... operates', which v2.3 rule 11 codes general_economic only; neither definition separately carves out conditions affecting the industry, so industry is not added.

m13holdout.correct_value: announcement_or_pendency, change_in_law, financial_markets, general_economic, industry, political_war_terrorism, stock_price_or_volume
m13holdout.reason: Clause (C) of the Prohibited Effect definition covers industry changes 'including legal and regulatory changes', which is a change in law or regulation (v2.5 rule 11), not the bare 'legal conditions' of v2.9 rule 6; change_in_law belongs beside industry.

Parent, which issues its shares and needs its own vote, owes the fee only on a Parent Adverse Recommendation Change, mirroring the Company's recommendation-change trigger, which v2.1 rule 12 and gold practice code reciprocal; a listed code fits, so other is wrong even though the amounts differ.

m13holdout.correct_value: announcement_or_pendency, buyer_action_or_request, change_in_gaap, change_in_law, compliance_with_agreement, credit_rating, disclosure_schedule_items, failure_to_meet_projections, financial_markets, general_economic, industry, natural_disaster, other, political_war_terrorism, stock_price_or_volume, stockholder_litigation
m13holdout.reason: Clause (viii) also carves out 'the availability or cost of equity, debt or other financing to Parent or Merger Sub', which no listed code covers, so it adds other; the extractor coded the clause but dropped that category.
